_comment: Two independent axes share this file, one row per collection, one entry per axis. RETENTION (MVP1.G3-CI-8, check_data_lifecycle_coverage.js): classification is one of DELETE / EXPORT / BOTH / EXEMPT -- DELETE means covered by deleteAccount, EXPORT means covered by exportAccountData, BOTH means both, EXEMPT means neither applies and why. ACCESS CONTROL (P2-ACCESS-1, check_data_access_policy.js): `clientAccess` is an array of {path, access, conditionalRefs?} entries -- `path` is the full firestore.rules-shaped path (one entry even when there is exactly one path, for one shape to maintain), `access` gives each of read/create/update/delete exactly one of NONE / OWNER / AUTHENTICATED / PUBLIC / CONDITIONAL, and `conditionalRefs` names the emulator test proving each CONDITIONAL cell (required, and only valid, there). See scripts/ci/DATA_ACCESS_POLICY_DESIGN.md for the full design and scripts/ci/lib/rules_parser.js for how PLAIN_OWNER/NON_TRIVIAL is decided from firestore.rules itself. Every collection discovered by EITHER checker's own discovery (firestore.rules match-blocks UNION literal .collection('name') calls in production source UNION registered path-registry exports, see the access checker for the third source) must have an entry here, both axes required. `users` itself is intentionally absent -- it is the root container, not a distinct data class; every subcollection under it is classified individually below.

accountDeletionRetries.reason: Deletion bookkeeping, not user content: durable deletion intent, one document per uid, written by functions/src/index.ts deleteAccount (recordAccountDeletionIntent) after the first sweep and BEFORE the Auth user is deleted (if the write fails the Auth user is not deleted). Holds ONLY uid (doc id), status (pending | failed_terminal), attempts, createdAt, nextAttemptAt, expireAt and, once a sweep has failed, lastErrorCode (bare code, never a message) -- no profile, email or payload data, so there is nothing to export. Lifecycle: written Admin-SDK-only; a clean final sweep in deleteAccount deletes the record (best effort); otherwise the scheduled reconcileAccountDeletions (every 15 min) claims the attempt first (attempts + 1, backoff) and then re-runs the shared sweep, DELETING the record on success (no uid retained); a failed_terminal record (12 attempts, ERROR event account_deletion_reconcile_exhausted) is kept for operator follow-up; every record is removed by the Firestore TTL policy on expireAt (createdAt + 30 days, firestore.indexes.json fieldOverrides). Not removed by deleteAccount's own recursiveDelete sweep by design: it must outlive the Auth user.

_canary.reason: Not real user data -- the synthetic runtime-monitor identity's own namespace (firestore.rules' isCanaryToken()/_canary block, MVP1.G3 Step 9A, functions/src/canary_probe.ts). Top-level, not nested under users/, so deleteAccount's recursiveDelete never touches it; the probe writes and deletes its own single document within one call, so nothing durable is expected to accumulate there for exportAccountData to miss.

read.testName: CONDITIONAL cell _canary/read: the canary identity can read its own document

create.testName: CONDITIONAL cell _canary/create: the canary identity can create its own document

update.testName: CONDITIONAL cell _canary/update: the canary identity can update its own document

delete.testName: CONDITIONAL cell _canary/delete: the canary identity can delete its own document

coach_bookings.reason: Top-level, keyed by clientUid/coachUid. Deleted via sweepSharedRecords (functions/src/index.ts ~1989-1991, queried by both uid fields). Exported redacted, both sides merged and de-duplicated (account_export.ts, BOOKING_SELF_FIELDS allow-list).

coach_listings.reason: Top-level, one doc per coach uid. Deleted via recursiveDelete (index.ts ~2155). Exported via account_export.ts's `one(coach_listings/${uid})`. Previously had no firestore.rules entry at all (fixed as part of building this check -- see firestore.rules' own comment on that block).

debug_sessions.reason: Top-level, written only by the sanitising callable sendDebugTelemetry (Admin SDK; clients cannot create, S02-09) with a uid field. Deleted via sweepSharedRecords. Exported via account_export.ts's `owned("debug_sessions", "uid", uid, ...)`, capped at MAX_ROWS.

donor_wall.reason: Top-level, one doc per donor uid. Deleted on opt-out and on account deletion (index.ts ~2154). Exported via account_export.ts's `one(donor_wall/${uid})`.

equipment.reason: Shared, client-read-only equipment catalog (firestore.rules:151-154). Not user-specific -- the same documents serve every user. Admin-tooling-managed; no per-user data to delete or export.

equipment_assets.reason: P1 equipment-identity shared catalog (media/asset records), server/admin-only. Not user-specific.

equipment_brands.reason: P1 equipment-identity shared catalog (brand entities), server/admin-only. Not user-specific.

equipment_catalog_active.reason: P1 equipment-identity shared catalog pointer doc (currently-active version). Not user-specific.

equipment_catalog_publish_jobs.reason: P1 equipment-identity shared catalog admin metadata (publish-job tracking). Not user-specific.

equipment_catalog_versions.reason: P1 equipment-identity shared catalog version manifests. Not user-specific.

equipment_external_mappings.reason: P1 equipment-identity shared catalog (external source-id mappings). Not user-specific.

equipment_identity_sessions.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid} -- automatically covered by deleteAccount's recursiveDelete cascade. EXPORT GAP: needs follow-up. functions-equipment-identity/src/p2/session_repository.ts writes these documents today (tx.set of pending/superseded/resolved session records), so live per-user data exists that exportAccountData does not return (it lives in a different functions package). Classification stays DELETE because BOTH would claim an export that does not exist; reclassify to BOTH once an export path is added or the content is explicitly judged exempt.

equipment_identity_telemetry.reason: EXPORT GAP: needs follow-up. functions-equipment-identity/src/p2/telemetry_repository.ts writes these documents today (server terminal telemetry and mobile telemetry fragments), so live per-user data exists that exportAccountData does not return. DELETE-covered by the recursiveDelete cascade. Latency/outcome counts may be judged exempt from export, but that decision has not been made; classification stays DELETE until it is (BOTH or EXEMPT with a rationale).

equipment_model_setup_specs.reason: P1 equipment-identity shared catalog (per-model setup specs), server/admin-only. Not user-specific.

equipment_models.reason: P1 equipment-identity shared catalog (model entities), server/admin-only. Not user-specific.

equipment_product_lines.reason: P1 equipment-identity shared catalog (product-line entities), server/admin-only. Not user-specific.

equipment_reports.reason: Top-level, written via reportEquipment with a reporterUid field. Deleted via sweepSharedRecords. Exported via account_export.ts's `owned("equipment_reports", "reporterUid", uid, ...)`, capped at MAX_ROWS.

equipment_setup_notes.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid}. DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade. EXPORT was missing entirely until this gate -- found by building this checker, fixed in the same commit (account_export.ts now reads it via sub(uid, "equipment_setup_notes", truncated)).

equipment_sources.reason: P1 equipment-identity shared catalog (ingestion-source metadata), server/admin-only. Not user-specific.

exercises.reason: Shared, client-read-only exercise catalog (firestore.rules:155-158). Not user-specific, admin-tooling-managed.

generated_exercises.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid} (cached AI-generated exercise lists). DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade. Exported via account_export.ts's sub(uid, "generated_exercises", truncated).

gyms.reason: Shared gym registry for QR-scan resolution (firestore.rules:163-166). Not user-specific, admin-tooling-managed.

machine_cards.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid} (per-machine cards from repeated scans). DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade. Exported via account_export.ts's sub(uid, "machine_cards", truncated).

profile.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid}/profile/main (onboarding/health questionnaire, health fields server-stripped). DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade. Exported via account_export.ts's one(users/${uid}/profile/main).

create.testName: CONDITIONAL cell profile/create: a stripped health block is accepted, a real one is refused

update.testName: CONDITIONAL cell profile/update: a stripped-health patch is accepted, a real one is refused

programmes.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid} (saved/generated training programmes). DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade. Exported via account_export.ts's sub(uid, "programmes", truncated).

receipts.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid}/receipts/{year} (server-generated annual billing receipts -- index.ts's own comment calls this 'the one document a user might hand to a tax authority'). DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade. EXPORT was missing entirely until this gate -- found by building this checker, fixed in the same commit.

recognised_equipment.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid} (AI-recognition history, one doc per equipment id). DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade. Exported via account_export.ts's sub(uid, "recognised_equipment", truncated).

recognised_models.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid}, server-written only (P1.G1 exact-model recognitions). DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade. Not yet wired to a live Admin SDK writer in functions-equipment-identity/src -- no data today requiring export. Reclassify to BOTH once a real writer exists.

scheduled_sessions.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid} (planned future workout sessions). DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade. Exported via account_export.ts's sub(uid, "scheduled_sessions", truncated).

stats.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid}/stats holding two docs: stats/workouts (all-time workout totals) and stats/workout_sessions (session totals written by the mobile firestore_workout_session_repository). DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade. Exported via account_export.ts's one(users/${uid}/stats/workouts) and one(users/${uid}/stats/workout_sessions).

subscription.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid}/subscription/main (Stripe-authored subscription state). DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade -- the Stripe subscription itself is separately cancelled by deleteAccount's listAllSubscriptions step before the Firestore sweep. Exported via account_export.ts's one(users/${uid}/subscription/main).

usage.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid}/usage/{day} -- server-side daily rate-limit/quota counters (abuse_guard.ts's enforceDailyQuota). DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade. Deliberately EXEMPT from export: purely operational metadata regenerated daily, no user-recognisable content, closed to client reads for the same reason (firestore.rules:63-65's own comment).

workout_logs.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid} (individual logged workout entries). DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade. Exported via account_export.ts's sub(uid, "workout_logs", truncated).

workout_sessions.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid} (in-progress/completed workout session records). DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade. Exported via account_export.ts's sub(uid, "workout_sessions", truncated).

body_scans.reason: Body scan records. Subcollection under users/{uid}. DELETE-covered by the recursiveDelete cascade (design 20.2). Exported by account_export.ts, newest first and paged by the app (D-61, C25). Client create and delete are refused (server-written, tombstoned); client update is limited to weightKg and clientNote. Photos in the private bucket are removed by the sweepAccountData prefix delete (D-60) and exported as metadata only.

update.testName: CONDITIONAL cell body_scans/update: an owner edit of only weightKg and clientNote is accepted, a server-owned key is refused

body_scan_settings.reason: Body scan settings (consent, retention, reminder), one document `main`. Subcollection under users/{uid}. DELETE-covered by the recursiveDelete cascade (design 20.2). Exported by account_export.ts, newest first and paged by the app (D-61, C25).

create.testName: CONDITIONAL cell body_scan_settings/create: a valid main settings document is accepted, an unknown key or docId is refused

update.testName: CONDITIONAL cell body_scan_settings/update: an unchanged consent write is accepted, a forged consent timestamp is refused

weight_entries.reason: Daily body weight entries keyed yyyy-MM-dd. Subcollection under users/{uid}. DELETE-covered by the recursiveDelete cascade (design 20.2). Exported by account_export.ts, newest first and paged by the app (D-61, C25).

create.testName: CONDITIONAL cell weight_entries/create: a valid weight entry is accepted, an out-of-range or malformed one is refused

update.testName: CONDITIONAL cell weight_entries/update: an overwrite of the same day is accepted, an invalid overwrite is refused

nutrition_plan.reason: Nutrition plan, one document `main`; update must carry planVersion + 1. Subcollection under users/{uid}. DELETE-covered by the recursiveDelete cascade (design 20.2). Exported by account_export.ts, newest first and paged by the app (D-61, C25).

create.testName: CONDITIONAL cell nutrition_plan/create: a valid plan is accepted, referProfessional and unknown keys are refused

update.testName: CONDITIONAL cell nutrition_plan/update: an update with planVersion + 1 is accepted, any other version is refused

nutrition_plan_reviews.reason: Weekly review records, immutable once written. Subcollection under users/{uid}. DELETE-covered by the recursiveDelete cascade (design 20.2). Exported by account_export.ts, newest first and paged by the app (D-61, C25).

create.testName: CONDITIONAL cell nutrition_plan_reviews/create: a valid review is accepted, an unknown decision is refused

food_entries.reason: Food diary entries. Subcollection under users/{uid}. DELETE-covered by the recursiveDelete cascade (design 20.2). Exported by account_export.ts, newest first and paged by the app (D-61, C25).

create.testName: CONDITIONAL cell food_entries/create: a valid diary entry is accepted, an oversized or malformed one is refused

update.testName: CONDITIONAL cell food_entries/update: an edit of a diary entry is accepted, an invalid edit is refused

saved_foods.reason: User saved foods. Subcollection under users/{uid}. DELETE-covered by the recursiveDelete cascade (design 20.2). Exported by account_export.ts, newest first and paged by the app (D-61, C25).

create.testName: CONDITIONAL cell saved_foods/create: a valid saved food is accepted, an oversized name is refused

update.testName: CONDITIONAL cell saved_foods/update: an edit of a saved food is accepted, an invalid edit is refused

nutrition_cache.reason: Central cache of PUBLIC nutrition-database responses (Open Food Facts, USDA), keyed by barcode/id/query hash. Holds no user data and no uid; written and read only by Cloud Functions (firestore.rules: allow read, write: if false), so it is neither deleted nor exported per user.

body_scan_purge_state.reason: Purge bookkeeping (persisted page token and counters) written by the daily body-scan purge. Holds no user content. Only the transient `late_sweep_<hash>` records carry a uid, for minutes, until the 5-minute late-upload sweep has run and deleted them; server-only (firestore.rules: allow read, write: if false).

equipment_model_text_keys.reason: P2-owned derived lookup-key index (functions-equipment-identity/src/p2/text_key_index.ts, firestore_paths.ts's P2CollectionPaths.textKeys). Server/admin-only, same posture as the P1 equipment-identity shared catalog collections above -- not user-specific.

equipment_identity_latest_session.reason: Subcollection under users/{uid} (P2.G3: per-user pointer to the most recently pinned recognitionSessionId, firestore_paths.ts's userEquipmentIdentityLatestSessionDocPath). DELETE-covered by recursiveDelete cascade. EXPORT GAP: needs follow-up. Same status as equipment_identity_sessions/equipment_identity_telemetry: functions-equipment-identity/src/p2/session_repository.ts writes this pointer today (tx.set of latestRef) and exportAccountData does not return it; reclassify to BOTH or EXEMPT once decided.

activities.reason: Unified activity SUMMARY documents (S02 design 3.2, 4). Subcollection under users/{uid}; scalar fields only (no geometry, no list, no heart-rate value: avgHrBpm/maxHrBpm are not on the rules allowlist). The one client-writable activity path: the owner creates (rev 1) and updates (rev strictly increasing, startUtc and sport immutable) through a shape-checked block that is excluded from BOTH wildcard clauses (GPS-PRIV-071); create and update are also refused while the id is tombstoned or the account-deletion fence activity_account_state/{uid} exists. Client delete is closed: deletion goes through the deleteActivity callable so streams cannot be orphaned. DELETE-covered by the recursiveDelete cascade of deleteAccount (Step 2), and again by the late sweep's final recursive delete of the activity collections (design 6.1 step 5). Exported by account_export.ts as the paged section `activities` (newest first by startUtc, S02-07). The streams themselves are NOT in this collection (see activity_streams and the storage section below).

create.testName: CONDITIONAL cell activities/create: an allowlisted summary is accepted, a geometry key or unknown key is refused

update.testName: CONDITIONAL cell activities/update: a higher rev with an allowlisted summary is accepted, a geometry key or a rev that does not increase is refused

activity_streams.reason: Stream INDEX rows (state pending | stored | expired | deleted, objectPath, bytes, kinds, hashes, expiresAt hint, settingsGeneration, purge bookkeeping and bare error codes; never coordinates). Subcollection under users/{uid}; server-written only (Admin SDK callables, purge, reconciler); client read is owner-only and every client write is closed (excluded from both wildcard clauses, GPS-PRIV-071, so a user cannot forge expiresAt or objectPath). DELETE-covered by the recursiveDelete cascade and the late sweep's final recursive delete. The OBJECTS they point to (GPS streams, never heart rate) live in the private bucket under streams/<uid>/<activityId>/<uploadId>.json.gz; they are removed by deleteActivity, deleteAllActivityStreams, the expiry purge (user-set retention, derived at purge time), the orphan reconciler and sweepActivityStreamObjects in sweepAccountData (both calls of deleteAccount). Exported: the index rows are in the paged section `activityStreams` of account_export.ts (allow-listed fields, no bytes); the stream bytes are NOT in the export body (GPS-PRIV-052) but delivered through short-lived V4 download links from the getActivityStreamDownloadUrls callable (GPS-PRIV-053).

activity_settings.reason: Activity cloud settings, one document `main`: cloudStreams consent (grantedAt / withdrawnAt), streamRetentionDays, settingsGeneration, recomputePending / recomputeCursor and the bulk-delete job fields (streamDeleteJobId, streamDeleteCursor, streamDeletePending). Subcollection under users/{uid}; written only by the setActivityCloudSettings callable and the continuation jobs (server-side consent so a client cannot forge it); client read is owner-only, every client write is closed. DELETE-covered by the recursiveDelete cascade and the late sweep's final recursive delete. Exported by account_export.ts as the single document `activitySettings` (S02-07).

activity_tombstones.reason: Delete markers `users/{uid}/activity_tombstones/{activityId}` (deletedAt, expireAt) written by deleteActivity BEFORE it deletes anything, so a queued offline summary write or a late commit cannot resurrect a deleted activity (design 6.2, delete wins). Holds the activity id and two timestamps only; no summary, no coordinates. Server-written; client read is owner-only (devices read the ids to apply delete-wins) and every client write is closed. DELETE-covered by the recursiveDelete cascade and the late sweep's final recursive delete; otherwise removed by the Firestore TTL policy on expireAt (400 days), declared as a ttl fieldOverride in firestore.indexes.json (like accountDeletionRetries and nutrition_cache) and enabled when the indexes are deployed, a release prerequisite (runbooks/activity_stream_bucket.md). EXPORT DECISION: not exported (S02-07 change record: bookkeeping of the user's own deletions, ids and timestamps only, no content); the S02 design table said BOTH, so reclassify to BOTH and add an export section if the operator wants the ids in the export.

activity_account_state.reason: Account-deletion fence and late-sweep job, top-level `activity_account_state/{uid}` (S02 design 6.1). Deletion bookkeeping, not user content: holds the uid as document id plus fenceAt, lateSweepAt, authDeletedAt, lateSweepDone, lateSweepAttempts and a bare lastErrorCode; no profile, activity or location data, so there is nothing to export. Written Admin-SDK-only by deleteAccount (after the Stripe cancel and token revocation, immediately before the first sweep; authDeletedAt in Step 3b) and by the 5-minute sweepLateActivityStreams job. Deliberately outside users/{uid} so recursiveDelete cannot remove it, and deliberately WITHOUT a firestore.rules block (default deny to clients; the summary rules only read it through exists()). Lifecycle: the late job sweeps both bucket prefixes and does a final recursive delete of the activity collections, then removes the document at max(lateSweepDone + 1 h, authDeletedAt + 70 min); until then it must stay (it refuses callables and client writes).

activity_reconcile_state.reason: Cursor bookkeeping of the 5-minute orphan reconciler, one document `activity_reconcile_state/main` (reconcile.ts, RECONCILE_STATE_PATH). Holds listing cursors only: no uid, no activity id, no user content, so it is neither deleted nor exported per user. Written and read only by Cloud Functions (Admin SDK); no firestore.rules block (default deny). Reached through a doc() path rather than a literal collection() call, so the lifecycle checker may report it as an entry without a current code reference (informational, not blocking).

storageObjects._comment: Informational, read by no checker: the private activity-stream bucket (ACTIVITY_STREAM_BUCKET, design 5; GPS-PRIV-064, 065). Object stores have no Firestore collection to discover, so each prefix is documented here with the same delete and export statements as a collection row. The default bucket stays deny-all in storage.rules.

streams/{uid}/{activityId}/{uploadId}.js.reason: Canonical re-serialised GPS, altitude and speed streams (heart rate and other sensor kinds are rejected by the server's closed schema). Written only by commitActivityStream after quarantine validation. DELETE: deleteActivity, deleteAllActivityStreams (consent-withdrawal offer), the daily purgeExpiredActivityStreams run at activity date + the user's retention (object first, then the row is marked expired), the orphan reconciler, and sweepActivityStreamObjects(uid) inside sweepAccountData (Step 2 and Step 4 of deleteAccount) plus the late sweep. NO bucket age rule on this prefix (retention is per user, including 'never'). EXPORT: not in the exportAccountData body (GPS-PRIV-052); V4 GET links with a 15 minute TTL from getActivityStreamDownloadUrls (GPS-PRIV-053); on-device GPX and FIT export.

quarantine/{uid}/{activityId}/{uploadId}.reason: Unvalidated uploaded bytes awaiting commit (signed PUT URL, 10 minute TTL). Never exported (not authoritative, unvalidated). Removed by commitActivityStream (promote or reject), a superseding upload, deleteActivity, the orphan reconciler, sweepActivityStreamObjects(uid) and the late sweep (covers a PUT through a still-valid signed URL after account deletion), and by the bucket lifecycle rule (age 1 day, backstop; valid here because quarantine has no user-set expiry).
